newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel says no moves planned on forex.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel says no moves planned on forex.

text.p: The Bank of Israel is not holding formal talks with the Treasury or working on a package of proposals to ease pressure on the shekel exchange rate, a spokesman for the central bank said on Tuesday.
"There are always discussions going on at the Bank of Israel, but there is no package of proposals being formulated," a spokesman said.

His remarks come before a scheduled meeting between Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel and Finance Minister Dan Meridor later today. Sources at the bank and Treasury said they doubted the meeting would produce any concrete proposals.

Since mid-January, the Israeli shekel has been trading at the bottom end of its trading band against the basket of foreign currencies to which it is pegged. To prevent it from sliding under the band, the Bank of Israel has been intervening heavily in the local currency market.

On Monday, dealers estimated the central bank spent less than $100 million to support the basket rate. On Sunday a Treasury official said the bank had spent more than $1 billion during January intervening in the market.

The financial daily Globes quoted senior central bank officials as saying they were considering various measures to alleviate pressure on the Bank of Israel to support the exchange rate. Among them was a special tax on short-term foreign currency borrowing.

The others include widening the trading band, which now allows the shekel to deviate up to seven percent above or below a sloping rate, to as much as 12 percent; suspending further government borrowing overseas and increasing the reserve requirement by five percentage points.

Bank officials said they are also seeking a further 1.3 billion shekel cut in the government's budget for 1997 after Treasury officials on Monday said tax revenues for January were behind projections.
They said tax and other revenues were only 8.6 billion shekels for the month, about 500 million shekels below the amount forecasted.
